title: Value-driven expansion cadence and technical checklist — QBR + renewal tracker
body:
Purpose / scope:
This is a pragmatic, modular QBR + renewal tracker and outreach cadence intended to convert healthy hosted accounts into Dedicated or Private deployments and/or premium SLA bundles. Focus is on value (latency/cost predictability/regulatory fit) and a technical gating checklist so Solutions Engineering + CS can move prospects through a short, repeatable sprint.

Quick summary (1-liner):
Run a 6-week “Expansion Bridge” sprint: week 0 discovery + baseline -> week 1-3 technical validation and ROI proof -> week 4 pilot + QBR -> week 5 commercial terms + legal checklist -> week 6 cutover plan / kickoff.

Who this doc is for:
- CSMs owning accounts with rising token usage or SLAs needs
- Solutions Engineers validating Dedicated/Private feasibility
- AEs prepping commercial uplift offers
- Renewal specialists tracking conversion timing

Key signals to trigger the sprint:
- Monthly spend > $XXK and growth trend 20%+ MoM
- Consistent 95th percentile latency spikes > customer SLO
- Data residency / audit requests escalating (SOC2 plus region-specific needs)
- Repeated retry/failover incidents in hosted regions

Core play components (modular):
1) Pre-QBR health snapshot (deliverable: 1 page)
- Baseline metrics last 90 days: tokens, avg token latency, p95, error rate, top endpoints by volume.
- Cost-per-1k tokens estimate across modes (hosted, dedicated baseline, private baseline).
- Risk flags: PII handled, audit requests, availability incidents.
- Proposed expansion hypothesis (short): e.g., "Move heavy realtime endpoints to Dedicated-1 for 40% cost reduction and p95 drop to <200ms."

2) Technical gate checklist (deliverable: pass/fail items + notes)
- Model compatibility: current model in catalog? quantized variant available? (Y/N)
- Peak concurrency estimate and sustained throughput needs (ops verified).
- Max seq length and KV-cache behavior observed.
- Custom tool/function calling footprint and external network dependencies.
- Data gravity: where are artifacts? (S3, GCS, private VPC).
- Security controls: KMS integration required? Customer-managed keys?
- Compliance requirements: encryption at rest, audit logs retention length, breach notification window.
- Integration hooks: tracing, debug logs, distributed tracing headers.
- Fallback policy: acceptable model variant for degraded capacity.
Notes: mark items requiring Platform/Infra/R&D engagement. SEs should annotate effort estimate (0-5 days).

3) ROI micro-model (deliverable: 1 slide/table)
- Inputs: current monthly tokens, average latency (p95), hosted unit cost, dedicated reserved rate (committed), estimated quantization uplift, ops savings (fewer incidents), estimated revenue upside from better latency.
- Outputs: 12-month TCO delta, payback period, and sensitivity ( +/-10% usage ).
Sample quick calc snippet (for conversation):
- Hosted cost: $45,000/mo; Dedicated projected: $30,000/mo (after commit & quantization) -> monthly delta = -$15,000
- One-time migration uplift (SE effort + infra): $22,000 -> payback ~1.5 months.

4) QBR script & template (deliverable: deck + speaker notes)
- 5min: Situation — usage growth and current limits
- 10min: Evidence — metrics snapshot, incident map, cost run-rate
- 10min: Proposal — Dedicated/Private config options and business case
- 10min: Risks & mitigation — fallback plan, pilot scope, security attachments
- 5min: Ask — commit level suggested, timeline, kickoff owners
Speaker notes: call out required legal/ops approvals and typical gating milestones. Attach sample terms (SLA uplift tiers and what we commit to: p95 latency targets, availability %).

5) Renewal tracker (deliverable: living table maintained by CSM)
Columns (text format):
- Account | Current contract end | Monthly spend | Trigger date | Expansion hypothesis | Pilot start | Pilot outcome | Proposed commit | Commercial owner | Legal status | Next action (owner + date)
Example row line:
- Acme Corp | 2026-06-15 | $62,000 | 2026-01-12 | Move /chat endpoints to Dedicated for latency & cost | 2026-03-01 | pass (p95 180ms) | $40k/mo 12m | Liam Carter | NDAs pending | SE to run final perf test by 2026-03-10
Notes: this table should be in a Sheet for live tracking; include a filtered view for >30d to contract end.

6) Outreach cadence (commercial + technical flows)
- T-30 days to pilot: internal alignment -> SE kickoff -> confirm test harness + dataset
- T-20 days: pilot infra provision (dedicated staging), quick perf test, send QBR invite
- T-10 days: internal QBR rehearsal with AE + CSM + SE + Legal outline
- Pilot run (2 weeks): daily standups (15m) with customer; automated perf dashboards shared
- T+3 days after pilot: deliver QBR, update tracker, commercial proposal issued
- Negotiation window: typical 2-3 weeks; if legal hits SLA Addendum exceptions route to Escalations

7) Sample consumer-facing language (email snippets)
- Subject: "Proposal to reduce inference cost and stabilize latency for <product-name>"
- Body (short): "Hi <Customer>, we ran a 2-week pilot and saw p95 latency drop from 420ms to 170ms and expected monthly cost improves by ~30%. We recommend moving selected endpoints to a Dedicated pool under a 12-month commitment. Attached: short ROI deck and draft terms. Can we align on next steps this week?"
- Technical ask: "Can you grant the SE team access to a 24-hour trace sample and a representative 2M token prompt set?"

8) Legal/commercial checklist (deliverable: yes/no + owner)
- NDA or DPA updates needed?
- KMS / key escrow language required?
- Regional data residency clause?
- SLA appendix: target p95, remedies (credits), measurement windows
- Audit rights clause?
- Professional services SOW draft?
Tip: keep SLA appendix templated and only vary numeric targets per deal.

9) Pilot success criteria (pass/fail + metrics):
- Pass: p95 latency reduction >=30% OR monthly TCO reduction >=20% OR compliance gating satisfied for Private
- Partial pass: meets one criterion, needs follow-up (e.g., more caching, quantization)
- Fail: no meaningful latency/cost improvement or unacceptable integration complexity

10) Handoff & runbook for cutover (deliverable: checklist)
- Finalize commit and billing schedule
- Provision Dedicated / Private resources; validate certs and KMS; run smoke tests
- Promote model versions and route production traffic with canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
- Monitor p95, errors, cost delta daily for first 14 days
- Post-cutover QBR at day 30 with ops SLA report

Open questions / unresolved items (notes-to-self):
- We need a standard one-page SLA appendix for Private that covers longer retention of audit logs — ask Legal for a template.
- Pricing maps: should we pre-bundle quantized models into Dedicated offers or price as an uplift? Ops to model scenarios.
- Who owns billing reconciliation for committed usage overages? Finance? CSM? (make explicit in play).

Attachments / artifacts to create (action items):
- Template ROI spreadsheet (SE use) — ACTION: Evan to produce by 2025-11-14
- QBR slide deck template for expansion sprint — ACTION: Marisol to produce draft by 2025-11-10
- SLA appendix skeleton — ACTION: Legal ping (J. Morales)

Appendix: quick SE checklist for perf tests
- Use 2-3 representative endpoints, run 10k requests at target concurrency, capture p50/p95/p99 and KV cache warm vs cold numbers.
- Confirm quantized variant and run identical test for delta.
- Capture trace of one end-to-end request including any external calls for troubleshooting.

Sample quick risks and mitigations (for QBR):
- Risk: Customer has heavy external network calls causing latency — Mitigation: propose proxying or caching layer; scope out work in pilot.
- Risk: Legal stalls on KMS language — Mitigation: offer hosted-managed key with temporary exception while private KMS integration is scheduled.

Closing notes (tone):
Keep the conversation value-first. Many accounts respond faster to a clear dollar + latency story than to generic product features. Use the pilot as both technical validation and commercial proof-point.

Notes-to-self: this doc should live as a short checklist + linked sheet for the tracker. Convert to a Google Slide and Sheet; include automation for calendar invites and a tracker webhook to Slack channel #cs-expansion.
